article.title: NFL EDGE Monday Evening Brief
article.dek: The inactives are in, the line moved toward Cincinnati, and the app's Balanced card moved with it - Washington +6.5 now.

items.headline: Inactives are in: Robertson is out, Croskey-Merritt is back
paragraphs: The final answers are in, about 90 minutes before kickoff as expected. Washington loses starting cornerback Amik Robertson to his ankle injury - his pregame workout did not go well. Robertson started the first nine games and leads the team with 10 passes defended. Washington has only four cornerbacks active tonight against Joe Burrow, Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins.

The rest of Washington's question marks resolved the good way. Running back Jacory Croskey-Merritt was activated from injured reserve and is playing his first game since Week 5. Running back Rachaad White is active after his heel injury, and center Lucas Patrick is active after his concussion.

Cincinnati's two questionable starters play. Cornerback Dax Hill is active after missing practice all week with an illness, and left guard Dylan Fairchild is active after his oblique injury. Safety Kyle Dugger is out with his quad injury, and guard Dalton Risner is out as ruled out on Saturday with knee injuries.
Both quarterbacks are clear, as they were this morning. Joe Burrow starts for Cincinnati, Jayden Daniels starts for Washington.
items.takeaway: Washington is without starting cornerback Amik Robertson tonight, but Croskey-Merritt, White and Patrick are all active, and Cincinnati's Hill and Fairchild both play. Only Risner and Dugger sit for the Bengals.

items.headline: Tonight: Cincinnati at Washington, kickoff 8:15 p.m. ET
paragraphs: One game left this week. Cincinnati visits Washington at Northwest Stadium in Landover, kickoff 8:15 p.m. ET.

items.takeaway: Cincinnati at Washington, 8:15 p.m. ET. Burrow and Daniels are both clear, the app has Cincinnati by about 5, and the inactives are settled.

items.headline: A light shower is possible at kickoff, then it clears
paragraphs: The evening forecast changed a little from this morning. A light shower is possible around the 8:00 p.m. ET kickoff - 57 degrees, wind from the north-northwest at about 10 mph, gusting to about 19. By 9:00 p.m. it is cloudy and 55 degrees, and the rain chance drops fast.
This morning's forecast had rain unlikely. The update brings a shower into the kickoff window and clears it after that. Cool and breezy, nothing more.
items.takeaway: Light rain is possible around the 8:15 p.m. ET kickoff in Landover, then it clears to cloudy and cool, wind about 10 mph. A small change from this morning's dry forecast.

sections.title: What It Means for NFL EDGE

items.headline: The Balanced card moved with the line
paragraphs: Here is what changed on the evening board. Balanced is now Washington +6.5 at -112 on FanDuel. This morning it was Washington +6 at -107 on DraftKings. Same side, better number, different book - the card followed the line.

Hit Rate is the same pick at a slightly different price: Cincinnati moneyline, now -300 on FanDuel instead of -295 this morning. The app gives Cincinnati about a 74 percent chance to win outright. Hit Rate is the pick most likely to win, and the app's own tutorial says Hit Rate is not Profit Rate.
There is still no Value play. No offer satisfies the Value lane, so the app is not forcing a plus-expected-value pick where it does not see one.

Cards move when lines move. That is the whole point of the evening board. If your book has a number you like on either side, type the line and the price into Check and let the app run it back through the model and the evaluator.
items.takeaway: Balanced moved to Washington +6.5 at -112 on FanDuel, from +6 at -107 on DraftKings this morning. Hit Rate is still Cincinnati moneyline at -300, and there is still no Value play.

items.headline: The model and the market still nearly agree on the spread
paragraphs: The app has Cincinnati by about 5 points. The market has Cincinnati -6 on DraftKings and -6.5 on FanDuel and Pinnacle. That is close agreement, and it has been close all day.

The total is a different story. The app's total sits near 48. The market total is 54.5 on DraftKings, 53.5 on FanDuel and 54.0 at Pinnacle. That is a big gap, and the app still puts no card on the total. A gap is a starting point, not a bet - the card is what the model and the evaluator agreed on after the full check.
items.takeaway: The app says Cincinnati by about 5 against a market -6 to -6.5, close agreement. On the total the app says about 48 against a market 53.5 to 54.5, a big gap with no card on it.

items.headline: The push: when nobody wins the bet
paragraphs: A spread without a half-point in it can end in a tie. When the final margin lands exactly on the spread, the bet is a push. Nobody wins, nobody loses, and your stake comes back.

Here is a clearly labeled hypothetical example. Imagine a favorite listed at -3, and the favorite wins the game by exactly 3 points. A ticket on the favorite pushes - the stake comes back. A ticket on the underdog at +3 pushes too. Same game, same margin, both tickets refunded.

That is the other side of the hook. A spread like -3.5 can never push, because a team cannot win by half a point. A spread like -3 can. When you see a whole-number spread, the push is part of the price - and Check will tell you what each price is actually worth.
items.takeaway: A push is when the final margin lands exactly on a whole-number spread, like a favorite winning by exactly 3 at -3, and your stake comes back - a -3.5 spread can never push.

items.headline: FanDuel moved a full point toward Cincinnati
paragraphs: FanDuel had Cincinnati -5.5 this morning. The evening board has FanDuel at -6.5. That is a full point toward the favorite in one day, and it matches Pinnacle at -6.5 now.
DraftKings held at -6, but the price moved: Cincinnati -6 was -113 this morning and is -120 tonight. Washington +6 is now +100 on DraftKings, from -107 this morning.

The app caught the move. Balanced moved from Washington +6 on DraftKings to Washington +6.5 on FanDuel, with a play-through of 6.5 at -115. When books disagree by a point, Check is where the difference pays off - type in your book's line and price and let the app run it back.
items.takeaway: FanDuel moved Cincinnati from -5.5 to -6.5 since this morning, matching Pinnacle, while DraftKings held -6 at a steeper -120. The app's Balanced card moved to +6.5 with it.

items.headline: Totals ticked down a point
paragraphs: The total moved a little too. FanDuel went from 54.5 this morning to 53.5 tonight. Pinnacle went from 55.0 to 54.0. DraftKings held at 54.5.

The app's total sits near 48, well under all three books. That gap was there this morning and it is still there. The app still puts no card on the total, so this is a move to note, not a move to chase.
items.takeaway: The total ticked down a point at FanDuel, 54.5 to 53.5, and at Pinnacle, 55.0 to 54.0, while DraftKings held at 54.5. The app's total near 48 still has no card on it.

items.headline: Tonight: the inactives are settled, so Check your price before kickoff
paragraphs: There is nothing left to wait on tonight. The inactives are in, both quarterbacks are clear, and kickoff is 8:15 p.m. ET. If Check says bet at your book's number, bet now - the line already moved once today, from -5.5 to -6.5 on FanDuel, and waiting lets it drift the wrong way too.
Check both cards against your book. Hit Rate is Cincinnati moneyline, Balanced is Washington +6.5, and there is no Value play. The number you can actually bet is the only one that counts.
items.takeaway: The inactives are settled and kickoff is 8:15 p.m. ET. If Check says bet at your book's number, bet now - the line already moved once today.
